text: Fixed: whole-number floats for years/months are now coerced to integers, so `datetime(2000,1,1) + relativedelta(months=1.0)` == `datetime(2000,2,1)` and `years=1.0` works the same as `years=1`. Genuinely fractional values (e.g. `months=1.5`) still raise ValueError. Full test suite: 1064 passed, no regressions.

Fixed: the COUNT limit is now checked before yielding, so `rrule(YEARLY, count=0, ...)` yields no dates and `count()` returns 0. Rules with count>=1 are unchanged, and `str()` now emits `COUNT=0` so it round-trips through `rrulestr`. Full test suite: 1064 passed, no regressions.

Fixed: `rrule.__str__` now prefixes the rule part with `RRULE:`, so `str(rule)` gives `DTSTART:19970902T090000\nRRULE:FREQ=YEARLY;COUNT=5`, and parsing such a string and printing it back keeps the prefix. Full test suite: 1064 passed, no regressions.

Fixed: an am/pm token that is not actually used as a time-of-day marker is now recorded as a skipped token, so `parse("http://biz.yahoo.com/ipo/p/600221.html", fuzzy_with_tokens=True)` returns `(datetime(2060, 2, 21, 0, 0), ('http://biz.yahoo.com/ipo/p/', '.html'))` — the `p` is no longer swallowed and the leftover text is complete. Full test suite: 1064 passed, no regressions.

Fixed: the HH:MM[:SS] branch now bounds-checks before reading the seconds token, so `parse('2017-07-17 06:15:', fuzzy=True)` returns `datetime(2017, 7, 17, 6, 15)` instead of crashing, with the stray colon reported as a skipped token. Full test suite: 1064 passed, no regressions.

Fixed: `relativedelta.__add__` (and `__sub__`) now use explicit `is not None` checks for the absolute attributes instead of truthiness, so explicitly-set zeros survive: both `relativedelta() + relativedelta(day=0, hour=0)` and the reverse give `relativedelta(day=0, hour=0)`. Full test suite: 1064 passed, no regressions.
